newsitem.title: UK: Lonrho says no truth in Anglo option report.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho says no truth in Anglo option report.

text.p: Lonrho said it saw no foundation in a newspaper report saying that South Africa's mining powerhouse Anglo American declined to exercise an option to give it a 25.7 percent stake in the British group.
"There is no foundation whatsoever in that report," a Lonrho spokesman said.
He also disagreed with the conclusion of the Evening Standard's report that Lonrho's demerger plans would be thrown into confusion if Anglo would not raise its interest.
"The option issue would not affect the demerger," the spokesman said.
Anglo, which already owns 7.3 percent of Lonrho, earlier this year bought the purchase rights over another 18.4 percent held by Lonrho's chief executive Dieter Bock.
Bock, in turn, has a put option to sell his stake to Anglo.
Because of this right to sell it does not really matter what Anglo intends to do with its call option, the Lonrho spokesman added. The options remain open until September 1997.

Anglo said in May it was interested in having links with Lonrho because of its earnings contribution and possible cost savings due to co-operation between the mining operations of both firms in Africa.

The Evening Standard said Anglo's enthusiasm has cooled off after being told by the Ghanese government it would not allow the South African firm to take control over Ashanti Goldfields , in which Lonrho has a stake of about 30 percent.
A source close to Ashanti, however, said it was already widely understood Ghana would not allow any company to gain control over the gold mine, which was floated two years ago.
Besides a stake of about 20 percent, Ghana also has a golden share in Ashanti.
Lonrho aims to split itself in three and expects to make an announcement on the planned sell-off of its hotels business in about three weeks, the company's spokesman said.
Lonrho plans to severe ties between its mining and trading businesses later this year.
